Diminishing Musharaka: CFO Workbench

Contract, interim profit, payment schedule, monthly income amortization and rental collection. The bank pays its share to the vendor, and the customer's deposit is its own share.

Unsaved changes. Save the contract on the Saved contracts tab to keep them in the database.

Dates as DD/MM/YYYY or DD-Mon-YYYY. From the vendor payment to delivery the bank earns interim profit on its full share at the annual rate over 365 days. It is billed as set in Interim markup billing: in the first instalment, or spread equally across all instalments. Regular rent is the opening balance x annual rate / 12, paid in arrears from one month after delivery.

A reset changes the rent from the first instalment period that starts on or after its effective date, because rent for a period is fixed before it starts. The entered-on date is when the system learned of the reset. A reset entered after its effective date is a back-dated reset. Use "View as known at" above to see the schedule before it was entered.

Interim profit = outstanding bank share x annual rate / 365 x days, split by calendar month. It accrues monthly and is billed as set in Interim markup billing on the Contract tab: with the first instalment, or spread equally across all instalments.

Difference between the schedule as known on the chosen date and the current schedule.

Instalment 0 is the opening position at delivery. Unit buyout is the total payment less interim profit and regular rent. Units bought = unit buyout / unit face value. Buy-out price is the present value of the remaining instalments at KIBOR only.

Interim lines accrue before delivery and are billed with instalment 1. Regular lines equal the regular rent of each instalment. Unit buyout is recovery of the bank's share, not income.

Collections are applied inside each instalment as set in Receipt allocation (profit first by default). A receipt amount goes to the oldest unpaid instalment first and any excess carries forward to later instalments as advance. Receivable is billed less collections on instalments already due, so it is never negative; payments on instalments not yet due are shown as Received in advance. Unearned income is income not yet accrued: periods that have not ended, and instalments received in advance. Suspended income is income stopped on a non-performing contract.

Paid instalments and recognized income are locked and never change. The outstanding bank share after the last paid instalment becomes the new base. Overdue instalments are rolled over, and the schedule is not re-amortized from the original start date. Profit already accrued, and profit suspended after non-performing classification, is held as interim profit carried (separate from the interim profit charged between the vendor payment and delivery), is added to the new schedule, and is recognized only when cash is received. Collections come from the Rental collection tab.

Position at the rescheduling date (the same figures as the Rental collection tab, calculated for that date):

1. User login

All data in this workbench is saved in the database. Each user sees only their own contracts. KIBOR rates are shared by all signed-in users.

1. Create contract

New contract resets the Contract tab to the default inputs. Set up the contract on the other tabs, give it a name and press Save. Saving with an existing name replaces that contract (the database keeps a history).

2. Saved contracts

Open loads a contract onto the other tabs. Archive removes a database contract from your list; it is not erased. Check against database compares the open contract's saved schedule with the one on screen. Export and Import work with the browser library.

1. Daily KIBOR rates

CSV lines: date, tenor, rate (for example 03/12/2024,3M,12.10). Every rate starts as a Draft. A different person approves it, and only approved rates are used. A newer approved rate for the same date and tenor supersedes the earlier one.

2. Contract lock and revision

The reset dates follow the contract's KIBOR reset frequency and tenor (Contract tab). On a reset date the rate for the period is fixed from the approved daily rate of that date, and the contract is marked KIBOR locked, revision due. If no approved rate exists for that date, the last approved rate before it is used and an alert is raised. A designated person from Treasury or Finance and Accounts revises the payments and income before the payment due date. A revision changes only instalments that are not yet due: instalments already due, overdue or non-performing keep their current rate, and a revision cannot be made when no forward instalment is left. The revision follows the RC method: a new schedule version is recorded, the earlier version is kept, receipts already taken are not changed and closed months are not reopened. A manual rate can be typed in the row to override the daily rate.
